title: B and T cells on sequencing
set_out: Commission Met-A, the coupling and IAM-A on sequenced B and T cells against IAM-Atlas v2.1; build the territories' and Met-A's healthy bands on sequencing; re-read the leukemia study as sorted B cells.

sections.heading: What ran, and how each came out

entries.title: The leukemia study re-read as sorted B cells
entries.what: All 36 samples read again from their saved pieces as sorted B cells, the column the atlas, IAM-A and the coupling all hold.
entries.outcome: Re-sent after the first re-reads used a name IAM-A holds no reference for; the first re-sent samples read on every instrument.

entries.title: Every A score in the A-score database, with where Normal begins and ends
entries.what: The A-score database now reads every current-chain reading of the sequencing groups and every replay so far (1,592 samples), reference only where not scored; each row carries its reading's state and chain version, and the gauge's band where the bundle records one (IAM-A, coupling-A, the C-Score's limits).
entries.outcome: 150,771 readings on six instruments; Bands.csv gives, for each instrument, cell, platform and chain version, the gauge's band beside the healthy samples' own spread.

entries.title: Met-A on sequencing: over healthy Met-A of its own cell
entries.what: Two approaches recorded as not met (the atlas converted to sequencing units; the atlas's own sequencing columns, synthetic). The third reads a sample over healthy Met-A of its own cell, as the coupling gauge does.
entries.outcome: Its depth check: healthy samples center on 1 (median 0.9988) but the ratio falls with depth, so the next step reads every sample at one fixed number of reads per identity site.

entries.title: The IAM Sequencing Atlas: every CpG, counted
entries.what: A second atlas for sequenced samples, beside IAM-Atlas v2.1: each healthy cell type's level, spread, each donor's disorder and two noise maps at every hg19 CpG, from the 153 healthy sequencing inputs.
entries.outcome: Built by the one command over all 28,217,448 CpGs in 113 pieces on Google spot machines, after its synthetic met; each cell has reads at 97 to 98 % of all CpGs.

entries.title: Google spot machines join GitHub's
entries.what: Eight discounted spot machines beside GitHub's twenty, each launch price-checked, capped to delete itself, and logged with its cost.
entries.outcome: One healthy sample read the same on Google as on GitHub; the atlas's counting step took about 15 minutes.

entries.title: A megakaryocyte column for the sequencing atlas
entries.what: The plasma cell type the atlases lack, from two healthy donors, moved from GRCh38 to hg19 by a new chain step tested on a known answer first; a third donor is held back to test it.

open_at_turnover: Running on GitHub's machines: the B and T commissioning samples and the study's re-reads.
